helpWhat1.message: Dragnet keeps a list of the Twitch drop campaigns running now and how far along you are with each drop, sorted by when they end. It reads Twitch's two drops pages, Campaigns and Inventory, as Twitch shows them to you while you are logged in.

helpWhat2.message: It makes no network requests of its own: it reads only the pages your browser has loaded, when you (or a Full sync) open them.

helpVisitTerm.description: Help term: the quick read done whenever a drops page is opened.

helpVisit.message: Whenever you open Twitch's drop campaigns or inventory page, Dragnet does a quick sweep. On the campaigns page it opens only the campaigns it has not read before; on the inventory page it reads progress and the newest claimed drops, loading more history only until it reaches claims it already has. A small label on the Twitch page shows while it opens campaigns.

helpFullSync.message: Opens the campaigns page in a new tab, reads every campaign, moves on to the inventory and reads the claimed history as far back as the history setting, then closes the tab. It takes a minute or two; keep the tab in front while it works, since Chrome slows down background tabs. Use it after installing, or whenever the list looks out of date.
helpFullSync.description: Help text: what the Full sync button does.

helpLeave.message: If you leave a drops page before the sweep finishes, what was read so far is kept and the rest is read next time.

helpListIntro.message: Each card is one game, holding all of its current campaigns; click it to show its drops. A card's time left is for its next unclaimed drop to end, and each unclaimed drop shows its own. The popup opens only campaigns with a drop in progress or ready to claim, the full page opens them all. The coloured labels mean:
helpListIntro.description: Help text, before the list of sample labels.

helpUrgencyCritical.message: Ends within 24 hours. The card or drop has a red edge.
helpUrgencyCritical.description: Help text beside a red time-left label.

helpUrgencySoon.message: Ends within 3 days. The card or drop has an amber edge.
helpUrgencySoon.description: Help text beside an amber time-left label.

helpUrgencyLater.message: Ends later. Hover over the label for the exact end date.
helpUrgencyLater.description: Help text beside a plain time-left label.

helpBadgeNotConnected.message: Your game account is not linked for this campaign, so its drops cannot be redeemed. Open the card and use Connect to link it on the publisher's site.
helpBadgeNotConnected.description: Help text beside the "Not connected" label.

helpBadgeClaimable.message: A drop is finished and waiting to be claimed. Claim it on Twitch's inventory page (the drop's "Claim now" button opens it).
helpBadgeClaimable.description: Help text beside the "to claim" label.

helpBadgeClaimed.message: How many of the campaign's drops you have claimed. The bar turns green when all of them are.
helpBadgeClaimed.description: Help text beside the claimed-count bar.

helpDrops.message: Each drop shows what it takes (watch time or subscriptions) and where it counts: named channels, or any channel streaming the game with drops enabled. A progress bar appears once Twitch's inventory shows progress, and Claimed once it is claimed. A claimed drop stays claimed even after Twitch stops listing it.

helpDropsNotRead.message: "Drops not read yet" means Dragnet has seen the campaign but not opened its card: visit the campaigns page or run a Full sync.
helpDropsNotRead.description: Help text; quotes the dropsNotRead message.

helpSearch.message: Search matches every word you type against games, campaigns, publishers, drops, rewards and channels, ignoring case and accents. "By expiry" lists campaigns by end date; "By game" groups them, the game ending soonest first.
helpSearch.description: Help text; quotes the groupByExpiry and groupByGame messages.

helpButtons.message: Campaigns and Inventory open those Twitch pages. The funnel shows the filters, the gear opens the settings, the round flag opens the language setting and the question mark opens this help. In the popup, the arrow button opens the list in a tab of its own.
helpButtons.description: Help text about the top bar buttons.

helpFiltersIntro.message: Filters change only what is shown. Dragnet still reads and keeps every campaign, so changing a filter needs no new scan. The funnel button shows or hides them; a dot on it means they are open.

helpConnection.message: Show all campaigns, hide the ones whose game account is not linked, or show only those, as a to-do list of accounts to link. A campaign whose card has not been read yet is never counted as not connected.

helpHideComplete.message: Hides the campaigns you have finished.

helpHideSubDrops.message: Hides drops that need a subscription. A campaign with nothing else is hidden, and one whose only unclaimed drops need a subscription counts as finished.

helpGames.message: Check games in the list, then choose "Hide checked" or "Show only checked". With "Show only checked" and nothing checked, everything is shown. Games whose campaigns have ended stay in the list, still checked, until you uncheck them; Clear unchecks all.
helpGames.description: Help text; quotes the gameFilterHide, gameFilterInclude and gamesClear messages.

helpHistory.message: How far back the inventory read goes in Twitch's list of claimed drops, from 1 week to 3 months. Longer reaches older claims but takes more "Load More" clicks on a Full sync; a normal visit stops sooner, at the claims it already has. Claims older than this are removed from Dragnet's history.

helpIncremental.message: Twitch sometimes adds drops to a running campaign, and you may link a game account after Dragnet read the card. With this on, each visit to the campaigns page also re-reads the 3, 5 or 10 campaigns read longest ago (at most once every 15 minutes), so such changes are picked up over a few visits without a Full sync. Campaigns not connected come round more often.

helpAutoClaim.message: When on, a visit to the inventory page (or a Full sync) clicks each "Claim Now" button before reading the page. Drops are claimed only while an inventory page is open. Off by default.

helpInventoryCheck.message: Off by default. Every 15 minutes to 4 hours, Dragnet reloads an inventory page you have open (but not one you are looking at), or opens one in a background tab and closes it once read. It reads like a visit, and with Auto-claim on it clicks "Claim Now", so drops are claimed without the inventory open. Apart from Full sync, this is the only time Dragnet opens a Twitch tab by itself.
helpInventoryCheck.description: Help text: the timed inventory check; quotes Twitch's button, which stays English.

helpStall.message: On by default. Twitch sometimes stops counting watch time on a stream that keeps playing; reloading the page fixes it. While a channel tab is open, Dragnet notes its channel and game, whether it is drops-enabled and whether it plays (kept only until the browser closes), and compares that with each inventory read. When none of that game's drops in progress has moved for 20 minutes, the toolbar button shows "!" and the list names the channel, with a Reload stream button. Optionally Dragnet reloads the tab itself, at most every 30 minutes; after the chosen number of reloads with no progress it stops and links to the game's drops-enabled streams. It never picks or switches channels for you.

helpLanguage.message: Dragnet's pages follow Chrome's language unless you pick one here. The round flag in the top bar shows the language in use and opens this setting. Twitch itself must stay in English for Dragnet to read it.

helpSettingsSaved.message: Settings and the game filter are saved in Chrome's sync storage, so they follow your Chrome profile to other computers when Chrome sync is on.

helpLastScans.message: Last scans, at the bottom of the settings page, has a card for each Twitch page: when it was last read, whether by a visit or a Full sync, how many campaign cards were opened or how many times "Load More" was clicked, and any warnings. The dot is green for a clean read, amber with warnings, red when a warning stopped the read.

helpBanner.message: A red banner at the top means a read stopped because the Twitch page did not look as expected. Your stored list is kept as it was. What to do:
helpBanner.description: Help text, before the list of banner messages.

helpBannerLayoutTerm.message: Page layout changed, or no campaign cards found

helpBannerLayout.message: Reload the Twitch page once; it sometimes loads slowly or partly. If the warning stays, Twitch has changed its page and Dragnet needs an update.

helpBannerLocaleTerm.message: A language Dragnet cannot read yet
helpBannerLocaleTerm.description: Help term: the page language warning.

helpBannerLocale.message: Dragnet reads Twitch in English. Set Twitch's language to English (in the Twitch profile menu, Language) and open the page again. Dragnet's own language is set on its settings page.

helpApis1.message: Twitch's documented public API (Helix) is fine to use, but it has no data about your drops, so Dragnet does not call it today. Dragnet reads the drops pages you already open.
helpApis1.description: Help: Helix (the documented public API) is allowed but not used today.

helpApis2.message: Dragnet never sends a request to Twitch's undocumented GraphQL API. Heavy use of that interface is the kind of traffic that can get drops paused.
helpApis2.description: Help: no requests to the undocumented GraphQL API.

helpApis3.message: Only if you switch on Twitch page data (Settings, Danger Zone; off by default), Dragnet also reads, read only, copies of the GraphQL responses Twitch's own drops pages already received. It makes no calls of its own and reads no tokens or cookies.
helpApis3.description: Help: the read-only Twitch page data switch.

helpData1.message: Everything Dragnet reads stays in this browser. It has no server and sends nothing anywhere. It can read pages on www.twitch.tv only.

helpData2.message: Campaigns, progress and the claimed history are kept in the extension's local storage, a copy of what the Twitch pages show that rebuilds itself on the next visit or Full sync.

helpData3.message: Removing the extension deletes all of it.

helpAbout.message: Free software under the GNU GPL 3.0 or later. Not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by Twitch.
helpAbout.description: Note at the end of the help page; keep the "not affiliated" statement.

dangerHeading.description: Settings page section heading: diagnostics and deleting stored data.

twitchApiLabel.description: Danger Zone switch label: read the Twitch page data the drops pages load (settings.twitchApi).

twitchApiHint.message: Also reads the data Twitch's own drops pages load from Twitch's undocumented GraphQL endpoint, read only: exact times and progress, the claim history without Load More, drops the page reading misses, and which campaigns gained drops. Dragnet only copies what the page already received and never sends a request to that endpoint. Reload open Twitch tabs after changing this. Off by default.
twitchApiHint.description: Hint under the Twitch page data switch.

diagnosticsHint.message: Shows the Diagnostics button beside the filter button, a page that probes and snapshots open Twitch drops tabs, and saves a copy of Twitch markup Dragnet does not recognize. For troubleshooting; off by default.

diagnosticsTitle.description: Tooltip of the Diagnostics button in the popup and the full page.

wipeLocalHint.message: Campaigns, progress, claimed history, last scans and diagnostic captures on this computer. They rebuild on the next visit or Full sync, except claims older than the inventory still shows.

wipeLocalConfirm.message: Delete campaigns, progress, claimed history and diagnostic captures from this computer? This cannot be undone.

wipeSyncHint.message: Settings and the game filter go back to their defaults. With Chrome sync on, this also resets them on your other computers.

wipeSyncConfirm.message: Reset all settings and the game filter to their defaults, on every computer synced to this Chrome profile? This cannot be undone.

wipeAllHint.message: Both of the above: everything Dragnet has stored, local and synced.

wipeAllConfirm.message: Delete all Dragnet data, including settings and the game filter on every synced computer? This cannot be undone.

wipeFailed.message: Could not delete; see the browser console.

helpDanger.message: At the bottom of the settings page. Twitch page data also reads the data Twitch's own drops pages load from its undocumented GraphQL endpoint, read only (exact times and progress, the full claim history, drops the page reading misses); Dragnet only copies what the page already received and never sends a request to that endpoint. Diagnostics turns on the troubleshooting tools (off by default). The delete buttons clear Dragnet's local data (campaigns, progress, claimed history), its synced data (settings and the game filter), or both; each asks first.

helpStats.message: The Statistics panel at the top of the full page counts active campaigns and games, drops in progress and ready to claim, campaigns ending within 24 hours and 7 days, and claims over the last 7 and 30 days with a bar chart per day. Where a filter hides some campaigns it shows both numbers ("3 of 5"). Claims come from the claim history, which keeps only as many days as the history setting.

aboutDescription.message: Tracks Twitch drop campaigns and your claim progress, sorted by expiration date, by reading the drops pages you already open. It never calls Twitch's undocumented API.
